ledger.note: 1033-1034: the Scots take Strathclyde. 'Conquered by the Scots, most probably during the reign of Maol Coluim mac Cinaeda who died in 1034'; Cliopatria's row ends 1033 and its Alba shape of 1034 is Alba plus the Strathclyde shape. Owain the Bald, 'king of the Cumbrians (or Strathclyde)', fought beside Malcolm II at Carham (1018, perhaps 1016) according to the Carham page, which does not say what became of Strathclyde afterwards. Corrected on review: the region is the corrected 1028 shape (Kyle out, Cumbria in) and the counterpart is kingdom-of-alba. Rheged page: Cumbria stayed under Strathclyde until the early 11th century, then was absorbed into the Scottish kingdom. Alba's ledger 1034 takes only Cliopatria's 40-cell Strathclyde shape (and one Cumbrian cell), so the 25 Cumbrian cells here are in no Alba shape until norman-england takes Cumbria from Alba in 1092 (its ledger 4): for the Alba dossier's author.

wars.name: Pictish and Northumbrian war on Alt Clut
wars.outcome: Mocetauc 750 (Talorgan, brother of Oengus, killed); Kyle taken by Eadberht in 750; Oengus and Eadberht take terms from the Britons at Dumbarton on 1 August 756, the combined army perishing on the tenth.
wars.note: The page does not name the winner at Mocetauc; 'the ebbing of the sovereignty of Oengus' follows.

wars.name: Viking siege of Dumbarton
wars.outcome: Amlaib Conung and Imar besiege Dumbarton for 'some four months'; the capital seems to move to Govan afterwards. No frontier changes.

wars.name: Brunanburh campaign
wars.outcome: Owain of Strathclyde joins Constantine and the Vikings in invading England in 937 and is beaten at Brunanburh; no change of frontier on the pages.
wars.note: The Strathclyde page dates the kings' submission at Eamont Bridge 'on 27 July' (927); the Æthelstan page has 12 July 927.

wars.name: Edmund's invasion of Strathclyde
wars.outcome: Edmund ravages Strathclyde and 'gave the kingdom to King Malcolm I of Scotland'; 'Dyfnwal soon recovered it'. No border change is drawn.
wars.note: Edmund I page (opened 2026-10-25): 'In that year Edmund ravaged Strathclyde' and 'Edmund then gave the kingdom to Malcolm I of Scotland in return for a pledge to defend it on land and on sea'; Dumville and Charles-Edwards read it as 'granting Strathclyde to the Scottish king in return for an acknowledgement of Edmund's overlordship', Williams as Malcolm's overlordship of the area 'in return for an alliance against the Dublin Vikings'. The Edmund page does not mention Dyfnwal's recovery or how long Malcolm held it; the recovery ('soon') is the Strathclyde page's. No year for the end of any tie, so no vassal event is drawn.

notes: Five pages budgeted and used. The Strathclyde page's 'Established: 5th century' predates Cliopatria's 644; the Brythons dossier carries the earlier Britons. Cumbria is drawn in Cliopatria's Brythons row (20 cells at 900), not in Strathclyde's; the Rheged and Strathclyde pages put it under Strathclyde from about 900, so the shapes of 870-1033 are corrected to add it and the Brythons dossier should drop it. The page's 'early 10th century' (Strathclyde) vs 'around 900' (Rheged) for the Cumbria gain; the Eamont submission is 27 July 927 (Strathclyde page) vs 12 July 927 (Æthelstan page). The northern salient of 647-749 reaches 56.7 N although the page puts the northern limit at Loch Lomond; unverified for those centuries. Kyle (750) IS inside Cliopatria's shape (6 of East Ayrshire's 7 cells), so the shapes 750-1033 are corrected to remove it. Not recorded as events because the pages give no dated territorial result: the 945 grant to Malcolm I (recovered 'soon') and Carham 1018 (war entries only). Rulers omitted: no list page was opened. Counterparts: picts and dal-riata have dossiers; no dossier exists for Kyle, Ayrshire or Galloway as a polity. Quotation marks enclose strings the page-fetch tool returned as quotations; other wording paraphrases its summary of the page, which was read by WebFetch only (no raw page text). REPAIR 2026-10-25 (review eu-11-g): (1) Kyle is removed from the shapes 750-1033 (keyframe 750 adjust, 870-1028 corrections), and the two notes that called it outside the shape are corrected. (2) The 870 keyframe is the Clyde shape alone (valid 870-899); a new keyframe 900-959 carries Cumbria, and the 960, 980 and 1028 corrections do too. (3) Cumbria is now the union of the 20 Brythons cells and the 6 Northumbria cells (26 of the admin1's 30). The Brythons dossier should drop its 900 Cumbria row (its ledger 24 duplicates this gain). (4) The dissolve names kingdom-of-alba and the corrected 1028 shape. Alba's ledger 1034 takes only the 40-cell Clyde shape, so Alba's author should add the Cumbrian cells; norman-england's 1092 gain then has its loss. (5) vassal_start 927 (month 7) and vassal_end 937 with kingdom-of-england are added from the Æthelstan page (reopened), mirroring England's ledger 4 and 8; the end is the page's 937 invasion (confidence 2), England's own is confidence 1. (6) Not done, and why: the 945 grant to Malcolm I is not coded as a vassal tie because the Edmund I page gives two readings and no duration, and the Strathclyde page gives no year for Dyfnwal's recovery; the 750 loss to Dal Riata stays at confidence 1 (the Dal Riata and Oengus I pages are silent) and the dal-riata dossier has no gain to mirror it; no ruler strip, because the List of kings of Strathclyde prints reign years only for 633-816 and 859 (several marked uncertain, one entry 'a modern error') and gives death or floruit dates alone for the 9th-11th century kings, so the strip would have gaps of 160 years. I do not disagree with any finding.
